title: Quietly adventurous Egyptian vine leaves Wrap
description: A grassy and flaky Egyptian dish featuring vine leaves and double-rise-bread, perfect for those seeking a shojin-friendly meal. This dish combines the freshness of vine leaves with the comfort of warm bread.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
Slice the double-rise-bread into 1-inch thick slices and toast until lightly browned.
Prepare the vine leaves by rinsing them in cold water and removing the stems.
In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat and saute the chopped onion until translucent.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for an additional minute.
Stuff each vine leaf with a slice of toasted bread, a spoonful of the onion and garlic mixture, and a sprinkle of salt and black pepper.
Roll the vine leaves tightly and place them seam-side down in a baking dish.
Drizzle the lemon juice over the rolled vine leaves and cover the dish with aluminum foil.
Bake the vine leaves in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, then remove the foil and bake for an additional 10 minutes.
Serve the quietly adventurous Egyptian vine leaves wrap warm, garnished with fresh parsley or thyme.
